title: Numeric Patterns, Flow Diagrams and Input-Output Tables
seo_title: Grade 4 Numeric Patterns Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Investigate and extend numeric patterns looking for relationships or rules of patterns: sequences involving a constant difference or ratio, of learner's own creation; describe the general rules for the observed relationships; determine input values, output values and rules for patterns and relationships using flow diagrams and tables.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 numeric patterns worksheets: extending sequences, finding the rule, flow diagrams and input-output tables. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Find the rule, then check it on every number.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A numeric pattern follows a rule. Look at how each number changes: add, subtract, multiply or divide by the same number.
  • Check the rule on every pair of numbers.
  • A flow diagram shows input values, a rule and output values: 6 → × 4 → 24.
  • A table shows the same: input in the top row, output in the bottom row.

Examples

Example

4, 12, 36, 108, …

4 × 3 = 12, 12 × 3 = 36

Answer: rule × 3; next 324

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Only two numbers4, 12 could be + 8 or × 3. Check the next pair.
Adding instead of multiplyingFast-growing patterns often multiply.
Rule on the outputApply the rule to the input.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about numeric patterns?
faq.a: Investigate and extend numeric patterns looking for relationships or rules of patterns: sequences with a constant difference or ratio, and patterns represented in flow diagrams and tables.
The same number is added or subtracted each time.
Each number is multiplied by the same number.

items.q:
The rule is Subtract 75. What number comes next?

items.e: Use the rule on the last number: 775 − 75 = 700.

items.e: Multiply the last number by 2: 24 × 2 = 48. (Adding the same jump does not work: the jumps get bigger each time.)

items.e: 8 + 6 = 14, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 8 and add 6 each time. 8 is where the pattern starts. It is not the jump.

items.e: Each number is 100 more than the one before. 1 400 + 100 = 1 500. Only the hundreds digit changes. 2 400 changes the thousands digit.

items.e: The rule is −50. Go back one step from 630: 630 + 50 = 680. The pattern goes down, so the number before 630 is bigger.

items.q: How does this pattern change?
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so the pattern is decreasing. 5 000 − 250 = 4 750, 4 750 − 250 = 4 500. It is decreasing by 250 each time.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1 000 less than the one before. 8 000 − 1 000 = 7 000. 9 000 goes the wrong way. 7 900 subtracts only 100.

items.q: Start at 3 000. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Count back by 500s 4 times: 2 500, 2 000, 1 500, 1 000. 1 500 is only 3 jumps.

items.q: Which pattern follows the rule “Start at 2 000 and subtract 250 each time”?
One number in this pattern is wrong. Which one?
Which two numbers are missing, in order?
items.e: The rule is −120. 840 − 120 = 720 and 600 − 120 = 480. The missing numbers are 720, 480. 740, 500 subtracts only 100. Write the numbers in order from left to right.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: The jumps are −10, −9, −8. Each jump is 1 less, so the next jump is −7. 73 − 7 = 66. 63 uses only the first step (−10).

items.q: Anika counts back by 25s from 1 000: 1 000, 975, 950 … Which number will she say?
items.e: Counting back by 25s from 1 000, every number ends in 00, 25, 50 or 75: 925, 900, 875. 860, 905 and 940 do not end that way.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
2, 8, 32, 128, …
items.e: The jumps are 6, 24, 96, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 4 times the one before: 2 × 4 = 8, 8 × 4 = 32, 32 × 4 = 128. The rule is Multiply by 4.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
27, 33, 39, 45, …
items.e: Find the jump between each pair of numbers: 33 − 27 = 6, 39 − 33 = 6, 45 − 39 = 6. Each number is 6 more than the one before, so the rule is Add 6.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
20, 28, 36, 44, …
items.e: Find the jump between each pair of numbers: 28 − 20 = 8, 36 − 28 = 8, 44 − 36 = 8. Each number is 8 more than the one before, so the rule is Add 8.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
200, 185, 170, 155, …
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so the rule subtracts. 200 − 185 = 15, 185 − 170 = 15, 170 − 155 = 15. Each number is 15 less than the one before: Subtract 15.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
3, 6, 12, 24, …
items.e: The jumps are 3, 6, 12, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 2 times the one before: 3 × 2 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12, 12 × 2 = 24. The rule is Multiply by 2.

items.q:
Which rule makes this pattern?
75, 69, 63, 57, …
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so the rule subtracts. 75 − 69 = 6, 69 − 63 = 6, 63 − 57 = 6. Each number is 6 less than the one before: Subtract 6.

items.q:

1, 5, 25, 125, …
items.e: The jumps are 4, 20, 100, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 5 times the one before: 1 × 5 = 5, 5 × 5 = 25, 25 × 5 = 125. The rule is Multiply by 5.

items.q:

4, 8, 16, 32, …
items.e: The jumps are 4, 8, 16, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 2 times the one before: 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16, 16 × 2 = 32. The rule is Multiply by 2.

2, 6, 18, 54, …
items.e: The jumps are 4, 12, 36, so it is not adding the same number each time. Each number is 3 times the one before: 2 × 3 = 6, 6 × 3 = 18, 18 × 3 = 54. The rule is Multiply by 3.

items.q:

22, 28, 34, 40, …

1 000, 975, 950, 925, …

26, 35, 44, 53, …

5, 10, 20, ?, 80
items.e: The jumps grow, so look for times: 5 × 2 = 10. The rule is Multiply by 2, so the missing number is 20 × 2 = 40. Check: 40 × 2 = 80.

items.e: The jumps grow, so look for times: 2 × 3 = 6. The rule is Multiply by 3, so the missing number is 6 × 3 = 18. Check: 18 × 3 = 54.

items.e: Put 7 into the rule: 7 + 5 = 12. 35 multiplies instead of adding.

items.q: The rule is Multiply by 6. Which In → Out pair follows the rule?
items.e: 8 × 6 = 48, so 8 → 48 follows the rule. 8 → 14 adds 6. 8 → 56 is 8 × 7. 6 × 6 is 36, not 42.

items.q: What number went in?
items.e: Work backward. Undo + 9 with − 9: 30 − 9 = 21. Check: 21 + 9 = 30. 39 adds 9 again.

items.q: The rule is Multiply by 3. What is the missing Out number?
items.e: Use the rule on the In number above the ?: 7 × 3 = 21. 18 adds 3 to the last Out number, but the In numbers do not go up by 1.

items.q: The rule is Add 15. What is the missing Out number?
items.e: Use the rule on the In number above the ?: 40 + 15 = 55. 45 adds 5 to the last Out number. Use the rule on 40.

items.q: What number went in?
items.e: Work backward. Undo × 3 with ÷ 3: 27 ÷ 3 = 9. Check: 9 × 3 = 27. 81 multiplies again instead of undoing.

items.q: The rule is “Start at 15 and add 4 each time.” What is the 10th number?
items.e: From the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps. 9 × 4 = 36. 15 + 36 = 51. 55 makes 10 jumps, one too many.

items.q: A candle gets shorter as it burns. How tall is it after 5 hours?
items.e: The candle gets 3 cm shorter each hour: 24, 21, 18, 15, 12, 9 cm. 39 cm goes the wrong way. 12 cm is after 4 hours.

items.q: The rule is “Start at 200 and subtract 15 each time.” What is the 10th number?
items.e: From the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps. 9 × 15 = 135. 200 − 135 = 65. 50 makes 10 jumps. 335 goes the wrong way.

items.q: A SkyTrain comes every 6 minutes. The first three trains come at 8:04 a.m., 8:10 a.m. and 8:16 a.m. When does the 6th train come?
items.e: From the 1st to the 6th train there are 5 jumps of 6 minutes. 5 × 6 = 30. 8:04 + 30 minutes = 8:34 a.m. 8:40 a.m. makes 6 jumps.

items.q: A rain barrel holds 180 ℓ of water. Karabo uses 12 ℓ each day to water her garden. How much water is left after 7 days?
items.e: She uses 7 × 12 = 84 ℓ. 180 − 84 = 96 ℓ. 84 ℓ is the water she used, not what is left. 264 ℓ goes the wrong way.

items.q: Lerato makes a bead pattern. Figure 1 has 7 beads. Each figure has 7 more beads than the one before. Which figure has 63 beads?
items.e: Count by 7s: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63. That is Figure 9. 63 is the number of beads, not the figure number.

items.q: Picnic tables at Stanley Park are pushed together in a row. How many people can sit at 8 tables?
items.e: Start at 4 and add 2 for each table: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. 8 tables seat 18 people. 32 counts 4 seats for every table, but no one sits where tables touch.

items.q: A cedar seedling is 30 cm tall. It grows 15 cm each year. How tall is it after 8 years?
items.e: 8 years means 8 jumps of 15 cm: 8 × 15 = 120. 30 + 120 = 150 cm. 120 cm forgets the 30 cm it started with. 165 cm is after 9 years.

items.q: Ayanda bikes on the Stanley Park Seawall. She bikes 3 km in week 1, 5 km in week 2 and 7 km in week 3. The pattern continues. How far does she bike in week 10?
items.e: Add 2 km each week. From week 1 to week 10 there are 9 jumps: 9 × 2 = 18. 3 + 18 = 21 km. 23 km makes 10 jumps. 30 km is 10 × 3.

items.q: Each canoe holds 3 people. In is the number of canoes and Out is the number of people. How many people can 15 canoes hold?
items.e: The rule is Multiply by 3. 15 × 3 = 45. 18 adds 3 to 15 instead of multiplying.
